summary.text: 青 covers “blue” and “green,” but its construction is disputed. The sources connect its upper part with 生 and identify the lower part either as 井 or, in the traditional account, 丹. Although the bottom now resembles 月, Wiktionary explicitly says it is unrelated to the moon.

history.text: Dong Chinese assigns meaning to 生 and sound to 井. Wiktionary attributes to Zhang a different sound-based analysis in which both 生 and 井 have phonetic roles. The Shuowen instead combines 生 and 丹, giving rise to an interpretation connecting growing plants with color.

uncertainties.text: These accounts disagree about both the lower component’s identity and the roles of the components. Their disagreement leaves the origin unresolved. The recognizable modern shape should therefore not be turned into a new story about plants and the moon.
